run_cell.py.usage_notes: Place at meta/experiment/tools/run_cell.py alongside select_tasks.py (the default EXPERIMENT_DIR resolves to the parent of tools/). CONFIG points, all overridable via env: ACE_EXPERIMENT_DIR, ACE_REPO_CLONE (full-history local clone of open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector; every manifest base_commit must be present), ACE_CLAUDE_BIN, ACE_WORKSPACE_BASE. Prerequisites before scheduling: arms/ must contain corpus-manifest.json (bare list or {"paths": [...]}) and original-docs/, ace-docs/, naive-docs/; the manifest's test_command fields must be filled in (the scheduler refuses to start otherwise — the current committed manifest still has them null). Behavior notes: (1) the run invokes claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions so unattended edits/bash work; this is safe only inside the registered sandbox, which is also what enforces network isolation (--disallowed-tools only removes the WebFetch/WebSearch tools); (2) idempotence — result.json is written for completed/failed/cap_turns/cap_wall and those cells are skipped on rerun; infra failures write infra-error.json instead and are retried; (3) on cap_wall the harness JSON is lost, so usage/num_turns are reconstructed by summing per-request usage across assistant transcript entries; (4) docs-read metrics count direct Read tool calls on corpus-manifest paths (chars/4 of their tool_result content); Grep/Glob calls are recorded in files_read.json but only a Read on a corpus file contributes to the headline counters, and docs consumed via Bash (cat/less) are not attributed — this limitation is identical across arms; (5) diff.patch is `git diff --cached --binary` against the baseline commit after `git add -A`, so new untracked files are included and the patch is recoverable with git apply; (6) transcripts are located under ~/.claude/projects/<munged-cwd>/<session_id>.jsonl with a glob fallback and an mtime fallback for killed runs. The scheduler shuffles the full task x arm x trial cell list with seed 20260801, runs sequentially, skips done cells, continues past task failures, and stops on the first infra error.
open_questions: Is --dangerously-skip-permissions the registered permission mode, or should the sandbox instead provide a settings.json allowlist? The flag is required for unattended runs but should be confirmed against the pre-registration's harness section.

The prompt is passed as an argv element per the spec (`claude -p "<prompt>"`); very large issue/PR bodies could in principle approach ARG_MAX. If any selected task's prompt exceeds ~200KB, switch to stdin delivery and note the amendment.
Corpus-manifest JSON shape is assumed to be a bare list or {"paths": [...]} — confirm against the arm-building tool's actual output.

Headline docs-read metrics count only Read tool calls on corpus paths; if the analysis plan intends Grep result content on docs files to count toward docs_tokens_read_estimate, the counting rule in analyze_transcript needs a one-line change (currently Grep/Glob are recorded but excluded).
cap_wall usage reconstruction sums per-request usage from the transcript, which can slightly overcount if the harness retried requests; acceptable for cost accounting?
Should the scheduler also verify pinned.json's commit matches the arms (provenance check) before starting? Currently it only checks that the arm directories and corpus manifest exist.

Fresh-session hygiene: runs reuse the invoking user's ~/.claude (config, memory). If the pre-registration requires a pristine harness config per run, wrap the invocation with a dedicated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/HOME — not implemented.

evaluate.py.usage_notes: Place at meta/experiment/tools/evaluate.py (sibling of select_tasks.py); all data paths are derived from the file's own location, so run it from anywhere. CONFIG points: TARGET_REPO_DIR (env ACE_EXPERIMENT_REPO, default meta/experiment/repo) must be a FULL local clone of open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector containing every base_commit and reference_merge_commit; JUDGE_MODEL/JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS; GO_TEST_TIMEOUT_S/SUITE_TIMEOUT_S; MAX_*_DIFF_CHARS truncation caps; EXCLUDE_DOCS_FROM_JUDGE (strips docs-corpus file chunks from both diffs shown to the judge, because the ace arm's doc layout would otherwise unblind the arm — the rubric tells the judge doc changes were removed and must not be scored). The is_corpus_doc() rule must stay byte-identical to build_arms/run_cell; it re-implements the registered corpus definition rather than reading corpus-manifest.json so docs present at B_i but deleted by C are also removed, matching run_cell's replacement semantics. Workspaces are git worktrees of the clone (cheap, shared objects), removed after each run. Pre-warm the Go module cache (go mod download in each module at the pinned commit) so `go test` needs no network at eval time; the judge subcommand does need network (Batches API, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ant-auth profile). tests skips runs whose tests.json already exists (--rerun to force) and, per the pre-registration, evaluates status=completed only (--include-capped adds cap_turns/cap_wall). If manifest test_command is null, the suite falls back to `go test ./pkg` on packages the candidate diff touched, scoped per enclosing go.mod. judge is resumable: --dry-run writes blinding.json + batch-requests.json without submitting; --resume BATCH_ID polls/collects an already-submitted batch; collection is idempotent (dedupes on blinded_id+pass_n). Batches run at 50% price; results are keyed by custom_id, never position. Typical order: evaluate.py tests --manifest meta/experiment/manifest.json; evaluate.py judge --manifest meta/experiment/manifest.json --double-fraction 0.2; evaluate.py judge-report.
open_questions: Should capped runs (cap_turns/cap_wall) be scored by default? The pre-registration says 'completed' runs; the tool defaults to completed-only with --include-capped as an explicit override — confirm which set feeds the primary analysis.

test_command is null in the manifest schema: the go-test-on-touched-packages fallback for suite_pass matches the 'scoped to affected modules' instruction, but a fixed per-task test_command filled in before runs would be more faithful to §6(a) — confirm the fallback is the registered intent or fill in test_command per task.

EXCLUDE_DOCS_FROM_JUDGE=True removes docs-file hunks from both diffs to protect blinding (ace's doc layout is identifiable), at the cost of the judge never crediting/penalizing doc updates the reference PR made — confirm this scrubbing rule is logged as part of the registered 'doc-style tells scrubbed' procedure.

Reference-test copying takes only changed *_test.go files; if a reference PR's tests depend on new testdata/ fixtures or non-test helper files added by the same PR, those are not copied and the tests may fail to build for all arms equally — decide whether to also copy new testdata/ paths.
is_corpus_doc() must match build_arms/run_cell byte-for-byte; ideally all three tools should import one shared corpus.py rather than each carrying a copy of the rule.

Judge prompt embeds pr_body from the manifest, which for some PRs may describe the implemented solution in detail — same across arms so it cancels in comparisons, but confirm it should not be scrubbed further.

Blinding salt is derived deterministically from the registered seed (reproducible); if the salt should instead be non-derivable from public material, switch to os.urandom and store it only in blinding.json.

build_arms.py.usage_notes: Location: the task named the file "tools/build_arms.py"; I placed it at meta/experiment/tools/build_arms.py to sit beside select_tasks.py / run_cell.py / evaluate.py, and it derives EXPERIMENT_DIR from its own path (override with ACE_EXPERIMENT_DIR). Run order: `build_arms.py --workdir <scratch> --step pin|original|ace|naive|gates|preserve|all`. The ace and naive steps hard-fail until meta/experiment/manifest.json exists (temporal firewall). Requirements: git, bash, python3, the claude CLI (ACE_CLAUDE_BIN to override), the anthropic SDK with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or an auth profile) for naive/gates/preserve, and kit release tarballs under <kit>/meta/dist (run the kit's meta/publish.sh first, or pass --kit-tarball/--skill-tarball). Key mechanics: pin uses a blob-filtered clone (checkout fetches C's blobs over the network); ace does a local clone of the pinned checkout, runs the kit's own adopt.sh --migrate against the local tarballs (pre-moving any conflicting kit paths into .ace-migration-staging/ and telling the migration agent to fold them back), appends corpus-mirroring patterns to .ace-ignore so the checker sweep matches the corpus definition, then runs one headless claude-opus-5 session (--dangerously-skip-permissions, WebFetch/WebSearch disallowed, 800-turn cap, 6h subprocess timeout); --resume continues via the recorded session_id, and every session's harness JSON, transcript copy, and standard-priced cost land in arms/gates/migration-cost.json. Token counting uses the API count_tokens endpoint with the subject model tokenizer (claude-sonnet-5), cached by content hash in arms/gates/token-cache.json. Naive rewrites go through the Message Batches API with the registered treatment string as its own verbatim text block; a single corrective pass (rescaled targets, rewritten from originals) runs only if the total misses the ±10% band. gates enforces check.sh (lint.py is recorded but non-gating, since the registration names check.sh only) and the band; preserve uses opus-5 batch judges with a structured-outputs JSON schema, maps ace divisions via exact-path → topic/-prefix → unique-stem heuristics, and exits 1 with a repair worklist on any dropped item, unmapped file, or judge error. Note that claude-opus-5 rejects temperature/top_p, so judge and rewrite calls are not sampling-pinned; the registered seed covers local randomness only.
open_questions: Ace-arm corpus scope: the capture includes the kit's own governed docs (docs/standard/, docs/dictionary/, docs/templates/, tools/README.md) as part of the ace snapshot, on the reading that adopting ACE-100 makes them part of the docs corpus the subject may read. If the pre-registration intends the ace arm to contain only migrated counterparts of the original corpus, the capture filter needs a one-line change - please confirm.

Run workspaces replace docs only, so the subject never gets tools/check.sh or tools/lint.py in the ace arm; if the intended treatment includes the checkers being runnable by the subject, run_cell.py (not this tool) must install them.

Token counting uses the claude-sonnet-5 (subject) tokenizer for targets, totals, and the +/-10% band; counting with the rewrite model (opus-5) instead would shift the band slightly. I registered sonnet-5 in a CONFIG comment - flag if the pre-registration fixes the other choice.

The naive treatment string is sent as its own verbatim text block followed by the document in a second block, and the raw model text is stored with no post-processing (no preamble stripping, no code-fence unwrapping), to keep the treatment exactly 'no other constraints'. If a rewrite arrives wrapped in a fence or with a one-line preamble, that text ships in the arm - confirm this is the intended reading.

gates enforces tools/check.sh only; tools/lint.py findings are recorded to arms/gates/lint-ace.txt with a warning but do not fail the gate, because the registered gate names check.sh. Easy to flip to strict if the registration means the whole checker suite.

Ace preservation mapping is heuristic (exact path, topic/ division prefix, unique non-README stem). Files the migration moved in ways the heuristic misses surface as 'unmapped' flags (exit 1) rather than silently passing; a hand-maintained mapping file could be added if the migration produces many legitimate moves.

adopt.sh --migrate installs the skill into .agents/skills and symlinks .claude/skills only if a .claude directory already exists in the workspace; the headless prompt therefore points at the SKILL.md path explicitly rather than relying on skill auto-discovery. If your claude CLI version needs the skill in .claude/skills to load it as a skill, create that symlink in the ace step.

Migration cost_usd_standard prices the harness's aggregate usage at opus-5 rates; if the migration spawns subagents on other models, harness total_cost_usd (also recorded) is the authoritative spend figure.

analyze.py.usage_notes: Run from the repo root: `python3 tools/analyze.py --out meta/experiment/analysis --bootstrap 10000`. All flags are optional: `--out` defaults to <experiment-dir>/analysis, `--bootstrap` defaults to 10000 (0 disables CIs, useful for quick previews), and `--experiment-dir` defaults to meta/experiment (the CONFIG constant DEFAULT_EXPERIMENT_DIR). Dependencies: Python 3.11+ stdlib only for all statistics; matplotlib is needed only for figures and its absence degrades gracefully (figures skipped, noted in the missing-data appendix of both outputs). Makes no API calls; consumes the precomputed cost_usd_standard from runs.jsonl. Outputs: summary.json (all numbers incl. per-task pairwise values, decision-rule verdicts, break-even, manipulation check, and a `missing` list), tables.md (six paper-ready tables plus a missing-data appendix), and figures/{cost_by_arm,quality_by_arm,bootstrap_cost_ratio,bootstrap_quality_delta}.png. Deterministic: re-running on identical inputs produces byte-identical summary.json and tables.md (verified); every random stream is seeded from 20260801 plus a per-statistic label, so adding/removing one statistic does not perturb the others' resampling. Analysis conventions (documented in the module docstring and echoed into summary.json config.conventions): status=="infra" runs are excluded everywhere; cost/turns/wall stats are intention-to-treat over the remaining runs (cap_turns/cap_wall/failed included); completion_rate = completed/non-infra; test and judge stats cover only trials with artifacts, with coverage gaps counted and reported. Judge scores join directly on task/arm/trial when present, else via blinding.json (dict-of-dicts, list, or {"assignments":[...]} shapes accepted); multiple judge passes (pass_n) are averaged per trial before analysis. Duplicate runs.jsonl records for the same (task,arm,trial) keep the last record. Smoke-tested end-to-end on synthetic 6-task x 3-arm x 3-trial data including infra runs, missing tests.json, blinded-only judge records, and removed judge/migration inputs.
open_questions: Cost statistics are intention-to-treat over all non-infra runs (capped and failed runs included, since they consumed tokens); confirm the pre-registration intended this rather than completed-runs-only medians.

The registered cost-superiority rule ('ace/original task-median cost ratio <= 0.80') does not say whether it binds on the point estimate or the CI bound; the tool reports both verdicts (point_meets and ci_upper_meets) and the console recap leads with the point estimate -- confirm which is the registered decision.

Quality non-inferiority '5pp test-pass' is applied to BOTH suite_pass and ref_tests_pass deltas (and 0.5 to all three rubric dimensions), with the overall verdict requiring every evaluable component to pass on point estimates; confirm whether only one test metric (likely ref_tests_pass) is the registered component, and whether the verdict should instead bind on CI lower bounds (standard non-inferiority practice).

arms/gates/migration-cost.json schema was not specified; the loader accepts a bare number or the first match among total_cost_usd_standard/cost_usd_standard/total_cost_usd/migration_cost_usd/cost_usd/total_usd -- confirm the actual field name the gates pipeline writes and prune the candidate list.
Judge passes (pass_n) are averaged per trial before aggregation; confirm this pooling matches the judging protocol (vs. e.g. median-over-passes or treating passes as replicates in the bootstrap).

Pairwise comparisons and the bootstrap drop tasks lacking data in either arm of the pair (complete-pairs analysis); with heavy asymmetric missingness this could bias comparisons -- acceptable given the balanced design, but confirm.

The break-even per-run savings uses the median over tasks of (original task-median minus ace task-median); an alternative reading of 'original median - ace median' is the difference of overall medians -- confirm the registered definition.
